xqml-scope-classical-data-pqc-post-hoc-l: Section II.A p.2 ('restrict ourselves to learning tasks with classical data'; 'we only consider unitary transformations') and Section II.C p.5 ('We focus specifically on post-hoc local attribution methods') state the paper's own scope. Read in context.
xqml-taylor-infinity-definition: Section III.A p.9 defines Taylor-infinity as a generalization of Taylor-1 (Eq. 13-15), valid for degree-1 trigonometric polynomials (each input component encoded once). The value gives no sign for the second-derivative term. Eq. 14 and C11 have '+ (1 - cos)' and C3 has '- (1 - cos)'. A series check (sum of (-1)^(k+1) d^(2k)/(2k)! equals 1 - cos d) shows '+' is right, so C3 is a typo in the printed Proposition.
xqml-proposition-taylor-decomposition: Proposition 1, Appendix C p.18-19: stated with its condition (degree at most 1 in each variable) and proved directly (C5 to C11) from the multivariate Taylor formula and the parity identities C6/C7 for trigonometric polynomials. No cited result is used. Note the printed statement C3 has a minus sign on the second-derivative term, which the proof's own C11 and Eq. 14 contradict (typo in C3). The value gives no sign, so it is not affected.
xqml-qlrp-exponential-classical-space: Section III.B p.10 states the limit on its own method: exponential classical space, full classical simulation and storage of the intermediate state, and not scalable to more qubits. The paper qualifies the runtime remark with 'In its current formulation'; the value drops that qualifier (minor).
xqml-qlrp-open-questions: Section III.B p.10: 'Two important questions remain open', both stated by the authors (applicability to classically simulable circuits; adapting QLRP to hardware with intermediate measurements to cut storage, possibly with only approximate explanations). Matches the value.
xqml-qlrp-root-points-single-component-l: Appendix E p.27, after Algorithm 1: 'As a potential limitation, this algorithm finds root points which differ from the original point in only one direction...' with the stated reason about encoding-function geometry. Matches the value.
xqml-twinn-isomorphism-lemma: Lemma 2 and Lemma 3, Appendix D p.20: both stated and proved in full on the page (block multiplication of real and imaginary parts; the diagonal of M(H) is two copies of the real diagonal of H). No cited result is used.
xqml-twinn-feature-map-efficient-entries: Lemma 4, Appendix D p.21-22: the proof is the explicit entry formula (D8 to D20) under the stated encoding (one Pauli-X rotation per qubit). Each entry is a product of d single-qubit terms, so the cost is linear in d. Constructive and in the paper. Conditions match the value.
xqml-twinn-expectation-lemma: Lemma 5, Appendix D p.22: stated as D21 and proved in two lines from Lemmas 2 and 3, both proved on p.20. Self-contained.
xqml-twinn-requires-efficient-observable: Appendix D p.22: the paper states that computing the entries of M(theta) requires a decomposition as a fixed observable and a variational circuit, and that this makes sense when the fixed Hamiltonian and the local unitaries have efficient classical descriptions. This is a stated condition for when its own construction applies.
xqml-evaluation-metrics-definitions: Section IV p.10-11 and Appendix F p.27-28 define Q_A (F1: fraction of absolute relevance on the correct components), Q_P (F2: Pearson correlation with the mask) and Q_ROC (F3 to F5: AUC of the ROC curve of well-explained against wrong-explained fractions). Matches the value.
xqml-experiment-data-and-model-setup: Section IV p.10 and Appendix G p.28-30: 6-dimensional data, 4 classes, 3 main dimensions per class drawn from a Gaussian, others uniform, n = 1000 samples per class (Tables IV and V), 6-qubit PQC with Pauli-X encoding and strongly entangling layers, Pauli-Z on the first 4 qubits. The paper's own setup.
xqml-experiment-training-hyperparameters: Appendix G p.30: categorical cross-entropy (G3), PennyLane with JAX backend, Adam with cosine decay, and Table VI. The rendered Table VI shows learning rate 1, n_epoch 200, n_layer 5, batch size 1000, as the value says. The paper's own setup.
xqml-experiment-generalization-caveat: Section IV p.11-12: 'this particular experiment is synthetic in nature, and there is no strong evidence to believe the trends showed here would generalize to larger, more realistic scenarios.' A limit the authors state on their own result (the item's result_type 'setup' is a stand-in; true type is measured result).
xqml-no-quantum-advantage-in-xai-sought: Section V p.12-13: 'we do not search for quantum advantage in XAI, we rather contribute to the foundations of XQML'; full characterization of advantages is left to future work. The cherry-picking benchmark remark is attributed to Ref. [89]; the value reports it only as one of the authors' two reasons, which the passage supports. Scope statement.
xqml-outlook-future-directions: Section V p.13 states the scalability issue must be addressed by quantum-time and classical-space efficient explanation algorithms with intermediate measurements, and lists kernel models, other encodings (data re-uploading), larger experiments and explainability-based design guidelines as further directions. Authors' own statement of what is not done.
xqml-numerics-no-superiority-claim: Section IV p.10: 'Our goal is to display the practical application of our protocols, not to claim that quantum models have an advantage...' and Section V p.12: 'different methods perform differently for different tasks and under different metrics'. Both are the paper's own scope statement. Confirmed.
xqml-scalability-limit: Section V p.13: 'Arguably the main challenge we encountered is that of scalability... fully characterizing the Hilbert space... quickly becomes classically intractable.' A limit the authors state on their own work. Confirmed.
xqml-two-novel-explanation-methods: Abstract p.1: 'We additionally propose two explanation methods designed specifically for quantum machine learning models'. Section III p.8-9 names them Taylor-infinity and QLRP. It states what the paper proposes; no claim of performance. Confirmed.
gilfuster-barren-plateau-definition: Definition 2, Section 2.3 p.4: the paper's own definition of a Barren Plateau for a hypothesis family (Eq. 1, expected variance in O(exp(-n))). Matches the value.
gilfuster-dequantization-definition: Definition 3, Section 2.4 p.4: the paper's own definition of dequantization of a QML model. Matches the value.
gilfuster-pqc-simulation-definition: Definition 4, Section 2.4 p.4: the paper's own definition of classical simulability of a PQC function family, with the remark that it concerns the family, not a learning task.
gilfuster-gradient-based-trainable-defin: Section 4.1 p.7 and Appendix E p.21-22 (Algorithm 1): the paper defines gradient-based trainable as trainable plus a gradient-based algorithm that starts from random parameters and only updates by local steps. Matches the value.
gilfuster-vari-veryational-five-properti: Section 4.1 p.6: the paper's own list of five properties defining 'vari veryational' models. The value lists all five correctly.
gilfuster-variationalness-not-well-defin: Section 4.1 p.6-7: 'The concept of variationalness is not well-defined', so a proxy notion is introduced. The open question about strictly more variational models is in the Figure 2 caption p.6 (shaded white area).
gilfuster-theorem3-recipe: Theorem 3, Section 4.2 p.7-8, proved in Appendix F p.23-24. Conditions are in the quotes (Q in BQP and not in HeurBPP/poly, an assumption; a gradient-based algorithm that solves the optimization with optimal value one). Trainability is shown by the algebra F.5 to F.13. Non-dequantizability uses the assumption and the reading of HeurBPP/poly 'as explained in Gyurik & Dunjko (2023)'; this is an explanation of the assumption, not a theorem used as a step, so it is graded HIGH, but flag that dependence.
gilfuster-theorem3-proof-reduces-to-easy: Appendix F p.24: the squared-error problem reduces step by step (F.5 to F.13) to maximizing <W^dagger H W>. The classical hardness half rests on the theorem's assumption (Q not in HeurBPP/poly, 'ruled out by assumption'), which the quote carries. Conditional on that assumption; same flag as the theorem.
gilfuster-corollary4-construction: Appendix F p.24-25: explicit construction (adder register A on t qubits so that U-tilde^L acts like one U for L < 2^t; observable Z with a product of RX rotations). gilfuster-construction-detached-minimal: Appendix F p.25: 'a valid criticism of our construction is that the way in which we turn a computational task into a learning task is almost trivial' and 'it is the minimal construction necessary to prove the statement'. Matches the value.
gilfuster-learning-separations-rely-on-h: Section 5 p.9: the authors state that all their separations rely on computationally hard problems and that the bottleneck was computing a classically intractable function while the learning itself was easy by construction. A limit stated on their own results.
gilfuster-open-practical-relevance: Section 5 p.8-9: 'This raises an open question: how can we take our constructions closer to solving practically relevant tasks?' and the proposed direction. Matches the value.
gilfuster-trainability-definition-limita: Appendix B.2 p.16: 'The main limitation of this definition is that it can be difficult to apply in real-life scenarios', with the stated reasons. Matches the value.
gilfuster-dequantization-definition-limi: Appendix B.4 p.18: 'A limitation of this definition is that it could allow for very powerful learning models to be dequantized for relatively easy learning tasks', with the all-powerful-model explanation the value gives.
gilfuster-scope-supervised-learning-only: Section 2.4 p.4: 'In this work we focus exclusively on supervised learning', with unsupervised extension named as future work. Matches the value.
gilfuster-contrived-supervised-only: Section 5 p.8-9: 'the models we have designed could be qualified as contrived', 'planting the solution in the architecture of the hypothesis family itself', and 'we discussed exclusively supervised learning scenarios'. All three parts are the authors' own limits. Confirmed.
gilfuster-trainability-definition: Definition 1, Section 2.2 p.3 (also App. B.2 p.16): the paper's own definition of task-dependent trainability. Matches the value. Confirmed.
gilfuster-trainable-nondequantizable-exi: The narrowed value is better: Corollary 4, Section 4.2 p.8, proved in Appendix F p.24-25 by an explicit construction that fulfills Theorem 3's assumptions. The conditions are in the value (up to sub-exponentially many layers; Q in BQP and not in HeurBPP/poly, an assumption). Theorem 3's dependence on Gyurik & Dunjko's reading of HeurBPP/poly is an explanation of the assumption (flag as for Theorem 3).
pqc-setting-trained-perfectly-1d-input: Section 2.1 p.4: the setting bullets state that the training parameters are trained perfectly and ignored, and that the inputs are real numbers. The paper's own setting.
pqc-one-dimensional-input-restriction: Section 2.1 p.4: 'This setting is restrictive only in as far as the input is one-dimensional; the reason for this restriction is that this paper aims to introduce and demonstrate a concept...'. Matches the value.
pqc-state-prep-out-of-scope: Section 1.1 p.2: general state preparation procedures (Harrow et al. [15], Schuld et al. [12]) 'cannot not be studied with the tools of this paper', because they apply many operations with parameters from a collection of inputs. The paper's own scope limit.
pqc-minkif-definition: Section 2.1 p.3-4: the three kinds of operation (input-encoding Hamiltonian evolution, trained Hamiltonian evolution, parameter-free operation) and the name MiNKiF after the derivative relation (Eq. 4) realized in Mitarai et al. [13]. The paper's own definition.
pqc-hamiltonian-two-level-restriction: Section 2.2 p.4: 'we mostly restrict to 2-level Hamiltonians with eigenvalue difference 1... commenting on other spectra only en passant'. The paper's own scope.
pqc-lemma2-linear-independence: Lemma 2, Section 3 p.5: the interval statement is proved in the text (analytic function vanishing on an interval vanishes everywhere). The whole-line statement is proved in Appendix A p.9 via the Fourier transform of tempered distributions (delta distributions are independent). The paper calls it a well-known fact and gives short proofs. No paper-specific cited result.
pqc-spread-definition: Section 3 p.5, Eq. 10a-10b: K_a is the set of dot products w.a over w in Z_3^n, and spread(a) is half the number of nonzero elements of K_a. The paper's own definition.
pqc-fourier-rank-definition: Definition 3, Section 3 p.5, with Eq. 12. The paper's own definition. Matches the value.
pqc-theorem4-fourier-rank-le-spread: Theorem 4, Section 3 p.5: stated for any f satisfying Remark 1's Fourier form (Eq. 8) and proved in the text by grouping the Fourier terms by w.a. The proof uses only the form in Remark 1 (which is the item's stated condition) and Definition 3.
pqc-corollary5-proof-bound-from-spread: Proof of Corollary 5, Section 3 p.6: |K_a| is at most 3^n by definition, so spread(a) is at most (3^n - 1)/2, and with Theorem 4 this gives n >= log3(2r + 1) >= log3(r + 1). Complete in the paper; the value states the bound the proof shows.
pqc-open-approximation-bounds: Section 5 p.8: exact representation 'is an unrealistic scenario', and the most pressing task is lower bounds under approximation. Matches the value.
pqc-open-other-activations-and-circuit-d: Section 5 p.8: lower bounds for many more activation functions could be proved (as pointed out by a reviewer), and a circuit-depth bound would be interesting. Stated as open directions by the authors.
pqc-concept-only: Section 5 p.8: 'While we emphasize the point that this paper demonstrates a concept... there are a few obvious avenues to improve our results'. The authors' own statement of the limit. Confirmed.
pqc-linear-encoding-bound: Corollary 5, Section 3 p.5-6, proved on p.6 from Theorem 4. The new value is better: it carries the exactness condition (h equals an expectation value function in a neighborhood of x0) and Section 5's statement that the proofs rely on exact representation. The proofs cover exact representation only.
pqc-redundancy-lower-bounds: Abstract p.1 and Section 5 p.8: the new value is better because it adds 'our proofs rely on exactly representing a target function'. Both sentences are the authors' own statement of what is proved and under what limit. The value reports what the authors state, which the quotes support.
gili-setup-12-qubit-cardinality-task: Section III A p.6-7: 12-qubit QCBM with line topology, cardinality-constrained uniform target with k = 6, |S| = 924. The paper's own setup for Section III B.
gili-setup-optimizer-simulator-iteration: Section III A p.7: gradient-free CMA-ES, NLL loss, Qulacs simulator, random initialization, iMax = 10,000, 10,000 samples for evaluation. The paper's own setup.
gili-nll-cost-limitation: Section II B p.3-4: 'A limitation of this cost function is that it requires explicit access to Pmodel(xq)... prone to the curse of dimensionality'. A limit the authors state on their own cost function.
gili-generalization-definition: Section II A p.3: 'We refer to the model's ability to generate data outside of the training set that are still distributed according to the data distribution P(x) as generalization', and invalid samples are called noise. The paper's own definitions.
gili-fidelity-rate-coverage-definitions: Section II C p.5: Eqs. 3 to 5 define F, R and C from G_new, G_sol and g_sol, followed by the conceptual meaning of each metric (quoted). The paper adopts the framework of its earlier work [25]; the definitions are given in this paper.
gili-metric-requirements-limitation: Section II C p.5: 'F and R do not require a priori knowledge of P(x)..., while a limitation of C is that it requires knowledge of the size of the solution space |S|'. Matches the value.
gili-normalized-coverage-rate-definition: Section II C p.5-6: Eq. 8 (expected coverage), normalized coverage C~ = C/C-bar, Eq. 9 (the approximation C~ = |g_sol|/Q when Q is much smaller than |S|(1 - eps)), and Eq. 10 for normalized rate. The paper's own definitions.
gili-normalized-fidelity-future-work: Section II C p.6: a normalized F is 'non-trivial' because F has no ideal value that depends on epsilon; 'We leave the development of a normalized fidelity to future work'; the comment matters only across different epsilon. Matches the value.
gili-utility-definition: Section II C p.6, Eq. 11: U is the sum of the costs c(x) over P5, the 5% lowest-cost unseen valid samples; a lower U under reweighting than under uniform training shows the 'reweighting bias' is learned. The paper's own definition.
gili-evens-dataset-and-reweighting-setup: Section III A p.7: re-weighted Evens dataset (even number of ones), cost = negative largest bit-separation of ones, softmax reweighting with beta = 1/T or 2/T (T the standard deviation of costs), all-to-all L = 2 ansatz, epsilon = 0.1. The paper's own setup.
gili-deeper-circuits-needed-hardware-cha: Section III B 2 p.10: 'the QCBM requires deeper circuits in order to obtain good generalization performance, and this may pose a challenge for obtaining good results on near-term hardware'. A limit the authors state on their own measured result (true type: measured result).
gili-pc7-criterion-not-oversampling: Section III C p.11: the cumulative probability P(c < -7) is introduced 'as a method to ensure that we are not simply reaching the lowest scores due to over-sampling', and a model P(c < -7) above that of the uniform target is the paper's criterion for a learned reweighting bias. The paper's own definition.
gili-no-overparameterization-seen: Section IV p.12: 'In our study, we fail to see signs of over-parameterization... It remains an open research question'. The authors' own statement about what their study did not show. The 'might come to light' remark is stated as a feeling, which the value says.
gili-future-work-scale-and-classical-com: Section IV p.11-12: scaling up, portfolio optimization, more elaborate training for larger circuits, and comparison with classical generative models are stated as future work. Authors' own statement of what is not done.
gili-scope-discrete-data-only: Section II A p.2: 'we ultimately restrict our subsequent model definitions to networks that learn distributions with discrete variables', with the stated reasons. The paper's own scope.
gili-simulator-only-hardware-open: Figure 1 caption p.4 says the circuit is executed on a quantum simulator; Section IV p.12 states hardware and noise as important future work. The paper's own scope and limit. Confirmed.
giordano-szegedy-walk-definition: Section 2.1 p.3: the paper describes the Szegedy model it uses as a discrete-time, coinless quantum walk on symmetric bipartite digraphs, derived from a simple graph by duplication (Figure 2, Eqs. 1 to 6). The description is the paper's own setup of the walk, with the duplication step credited to [21].
giordano-marked-vertices-absorbing: Section 2.1 p.3-4: marked vertices are absorbing states with only incoming links (p_ii = 1, p_ij = 0). The paper's own modelling choice (Eq. 5).
giordano-evolution-operator-two-reflecti: Section 2.2 p.4-5, Eqs. 1 to 4: W_P = R_B R_A with R_A and R_B reflections about the subspaces A and B. The paper's own definition.
giordano-time-averaged-distance-definiti: Definitions 1 and 2, Section 2.3 p.6: TAD F(T) (Eq. 7) and the hitting time as the minimum t with F(t) >= 1 - m/n (Eq. 8). The paper defines them (credited to [21, 18]).
giordano-optimality-condition-definition: Definition 3, Section 2.4 p.8-9, Eq. 21: the Optimality Condition sets the hitting time equal to t_max(n, m). The paper's own definition.
giordano-spectral-radius-assumption: Section 2.6 p.13: 'Based on the analysis of the spectral radius of nonnegative matrices [26], and supported by our simulations in Appendix C, we assume this inequality holds also for the corresponding matrices'. The authors state the assumption as an assumption. Matches the value.
giordano-stage1-procedure: Section 3.1 p.15: the paper's own Stage 1 steps (m* = round((n - 1)/a), mark m* random nodes, run t* = 3 steps, measure, report not complete if the walker is on an unmarked node). Matches the value.
giordano-stage2-procedure: Section 3.1 p.16-17: the paper's own Stage 2 steps 5.1 to 7 (m = 1, |0>^p|theta_2+>, Hadamards, controlled powers of W, inverse QFT, measure, compare theta_j with theta_2). The preparation of |theta_2+> is credited to [27, 28], as the value says.
giordano-appendixb-normalizing-ansatz: Appendix B p.24: 'Although we do not have an explicit expression for N in the incomplete case, we assume a normalizing ansatz N~ such that N~ < N'. The authors state the assumption. Matches the value.

theory_low.xqml-table1-method-properties: Table I p.7 was checked against the rendered page and the value reads it correctly. It is the authors' own rating of existing methods against three criteria, with no proof or measurement. An authors' assessment, not a proved result.
theory_low.xqml-qlrp-linear-rule: Section III.B p.9-10 states the linear rule and encoding rule as proposals. 'Always conservative by construction' holds for the linear rule (Appendix E, exact by linearity), but the encoding rule is only approximately conservative and only with good root points. The paper gives the rules by definition and the optimization goal by assertion; no theorem. Authors' proposal, not a proved result.
theory_low.xqml-qlrp-conservation-assumes-good-root: Section III.B p.10 and Appendix E p.24: conservation is stated as holding 'assuming we have good root points' and the encoding rule is 'approximately conservative', with the amount set by the quality of the Fourier approximation. The condition is an unproved assumption and Appendix E offers an approximation chain (E7), not a bound.
theory_low.xqml-qlrp-root-point-algorithm-od-steps: Appendix E p.26: 'we need to repeat this process at most O(d) times' is stated in prose after a plain-language description of the procedure, with no proof. The parameter-shift remark (E8 to E12) is shown, but the step count is an informal bound.
theory_low.gilfuster-no-bp-necessary-gradient-train: Section 4.1 p.7: argued in prose from 'standard optimization theory' with a citation to Goodfellow et al. (2016) and not proved. The not-sufficient half rests on You & Wu (2021) and Anschuetz & Kiani (2022). A cited and informal argument, not a theorem proved here.
theory_low.gilfuster-bp-model-not-efficiently-gradi: Appendix E p.22-23: an argument in prose (exponentially small gradients are statistically indistinguishable from zero for QML precision) with no theorem or proof. 'For the same distribution P, a model that has a BP cannot be efficiently gradient-based trainable' is asserted from that argument.
theory_low.gilfuster-proposition1-proof-hea-lcu: Appendix D p.20-21: the proof of Proposition 1 uses two other papers' results as steps: Cerezo et al. (2021a) for 'this circuit has a BP' (HEA of linear depth with a global observable), and Liu et al. (2021) for the DLP kernel solving the learning task. The LCU construction itself is shown. Per the rule, a proof that rests on specific cited theorems is LOW.
theory_low.gilfuster-proposition1-implication-bp-no: Section 4.1 p.7: 'neither necessary nor sufficient' joins Proposition 1 (which rests on Cerezo et al. 2021a and Liu et al. 2021, see its proof) with the 'not sufficient' direction taken from You & Wu (2021) and Anschuetz & Kiani (2022). Cited results, not proved here.
theory_low.gilfuster-corollary2-deep-hea-trainable-: Corollary 2, Section 4.1 p.7: the proof is one line, 'It follows directly from Prop. 1 and Liu et al. (2021)'. It rests on Liu et al. (2021) and on Proposition 1, which itself uses Cerezo et al. 2021a. The training is not gradient based, as the value says.
theory_low.gilfuster-kernel-models-not-gradient-tra: Appendix E p.22-23: follows from the paper's own definition by a prose argument (the representer-theorem step is not an allowed operation), with no formal proof. Argued informally.
theory_low.gilfuster-fig3-implications-read: Figure 3 p.9, checked against the rendered page: the blue arrows run from gradient-based trainability to absence of barren plateaus and to trainability, and from simulation to dequantization 'with easy training algorithm'; orange crossed arrows are labelled with prior works plus Proposition 1 and Corollary 4. The value reads it correctly. Several edges are results of prior work (Anschuetz & Kiani, Liu et al., Cerezo et al., Gyurik & Dunjko, Huang et al.). A value read from a diagram is never HIGH on the figure alone.
theory_low.gilfuster-bp-trainable: The narrowed value is right: Proposition 1 p.7 and its sketch say the training is an SVM followed by fixing the circuit parameters, so not gradient based with respect to the HEA parameters. Grade LOW because the Appendix D proof (p.20-21) uses Cerezo et al. (2021a) for the barren plateau and Liu et al. (2021) for the DLP kernel result as steps. The statement is also conditional on standard cryptographic assumptions.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.pqc-remark1-equivalence: Remark 1, Section 2.2 p.4-5: the paper says the equivalence 'is contained in the above discussions, except for the existence of a quantum circuit for a given multi-linear trigonometric polynomial, for which we defer [17]' (the author's thesis). The Fourier-spectrum part also follows 'the simple observation of [16]' with 'the (easy) details' left to [16]. No proof of the circuit-existence direction in this paper, so the three-way equivalence is not proved here.
theory_low.pqc-fourier-rank-examples: The examples after Definition 3 (p.5) are listed without any proof, so they are stated, not proved. They are elementary (constants, cos(kappa x + phi), x, sin(pi x)).
theory_low.pqc-remark6-spread-depends-on-a: Remark 6, Section 3 p.6: the random-entry value is introduced with 'It can be seen that...' and no proof; the remark about choosing a, b depending on h is only 'plausible'.
theory_low.pqc-remark7-other-hamiltonian-spectra: Remark 7, Section 3 p.6: 'Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 remain valid, with essentially the same proofs, but with a higher base for the logarithm'. The proof is not written out.
theory_low.pqc-corollary9-arcsine-polynomial-degree: Corollary 9, Section 4 p.6-7: the proof uses Lemma 8, introduced as 'The following technical fact can be shown (cf. [17])' (the author's thesis), and Eq. 13 from the same thesis. Lemma 8 (the analytic continuation of a combination of sc-monomials of degree at most d is a polynomial of degree at most d) is cited, not proved here.
theory_low.pqc-no-arcsine-pqc-for-nonpolynomial-ana: Examples after Corollary 9, Section 4 p.7: they follow from Corollary 9, which rests on the thesis [17] (Lemma 8 and Eq. 13). The examples are stated in one line without further proof.
theory_low.pqc-proposition10-dimension-3n: Proposition 10, Section 4 p.7: the counting of at most 3^n sc-monomials is shown, but 'the fact that the sc-monomials generate the expectation value functions with arcsine input-encoding of redundancy n is just the statement of (13)', which comes from the thesis [17]. The spanning part is cited.
theory_low.pqc-corollary11-sc-rank-bound: Corollary 11, Section 4 p.7: it follows directly from Proposition 10, which depends on Eq. 13 from the thesis [17]. Also the statement writes the encoding as arcsin(x.a + b)/(2 pi), different from the earlier arcsin((ax + b)/(2 pi)) of Section 4.
theory_low.pqc-mitarai-redundancy-n-for-degree-n: Section 1.2 p.2 ('we leave that to the reader') and Section 4 p.7 (a one-sentence sketch via the Pauli transfer matrix). No proof is given; the general result is Corollary 9, itself resting on the thesis [17].
theory_low.pqc-bounds-logarithmic-tight: Section 1.3 p.3: 'the bounds are tight' is an introductory claim. No theorem or example in Sections 3 to 5 proves tightness; Section 5 says 'at least logarithmically'. The bounds also hold only for exact representation (Section 5). The passage does not settle tightness.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.giordano-prop1-linear-relation-a-1p44512: Proposition 1, Section 2.4 p.9 and Appendix A p.22-23: the appendix says 'We use a suitable ansatz for the solution, suggesting a linear relationship between n and m' and substitutes n = a m + 1 to get Eq. A.12 and a = 1.44512 (numerically). The paper does not show it is the only non-trivial solution. Uses Eqs. 18 and 19 from [21]. A solution found by ansatz and numerics. The value says 'the solution'.
theory_low.giordano-appendixa-trivial-solution-and-: Appendix A p.22-23: the factorization (m - n) Q(n, m) = 0 follows from Eq. A.2 to A.9, which start from the closed forms of F(t, n, m) and t_max in Eqs. 18 and 19, taken from [21], and some simplifications (A.2 to A.3, A.4) are stated without steps. theory_low.giordano-tmax-constant-and-second-maximu: Section 2.5 p.9-10: derived from Eqs. 19, 24 and 25 with the ansatz m = (n - 1)/a. t*_max about 0.3745 and second maximum about 2.8724 are computed values; choosing the second maximum because the first rounds to zero is an authors' design choice. I rechecked the arithmetic and it agrees. A derived value with a rounding choice, not a proved result. 'Three steps' is the rounded 2.8724.
theory_low.giordano-pm-limits-0p9389-0p9812: Section 2.5 p.10, Eqs. 26a and 26b: limits are stated numerically (0.9389, 0.9812) with no derivation shown. 'Remains consistently close to 1' is the authors' reading of Figure 3. Derived values stated without working.
theory_low.giordano-fig3-probability-curve-read: Figure 3 p.11, checked against the rendered page: the curve rises from about 0.94 at n near 1 to about 0.98 by n of about 25 and stays just below the 0.981 limit line to n = 200, so the reading is correct. A value read by eye from a plot is never HIGH on the figure alone.
theory_low.giordano-implication-logic-stage1: Section 2.5 p.10-11: 'Not finding a marked node implies the graph is incomplete' rests on P_M being approximately 1 (0.94 to 0.98) for a complete graph, not exactly 1, and the paper gives no error analysis for a false negative. The converse statement is sound as written. The first implication is an authors' inference with an approximation.
theory_low.giordano-prop2-completeness-indicator: Proposition 2, Section 2.6 p.12: the 'only if' direction rests on the assumption (stated p.13) that the spectral-radius inequality for adjacency matrices holds also for the transition matrices, supported by simulations in Appendix C, not proved. It also relies on spectral radius bounds from [23, 24] and the spectrum from [21]. The 'proof' is an argument in prose.
theory_low.giordano-worst-case-one-missing-edge: Section 2.6 p.13: 'for a fixed n, the closer |E| is to |Ec|, the closer rho(A) is to rho(Ac)' is stated from the bound in Eq. 30 and the worst case with one missing edge is the authors' reasoning, with no proof for the transition matrices.
theory_low.giordano-prop3-qubits-log-n: Proposition 3, Section 3.2 p.17-18 and Appendix B p.24-25: F(n) is not derived. 'Since choosing a suitable N~ is not straightforward, we fit some simulated theta_j - theta_2 data' (n up to 300, Figure B.5), with F(n) ~ n^3.4 adjusted to lie below the data. The log2(n) + 1 qubit count is a fit, not a proved bound, and the normalizing ansatz N~ < N is assumed. O(log2 n) also counts only the inverse QFT.
theory_low.stage1-constant-three-steps: The narrowed value is better: the constant 3 is the integer nearest the second maximum t*_max + pi/arccos((a-1)/a), about 2.8724 (Eq. 25, Section 2.5 p.10), chosen because the first maximum about 0.3745 rounds to zero. It is the authors' own derivation with a rounding step, for a complete graph with m* marked nodes, so LOW. 'Tends to' is as stated in Section 1 p.2. Version v3.
